proposal.analysis: The positives consistently show a unique two-loop point contact with strongly unequal cross-owner exterior openings: one visibly narrow gap and one broad gap. The nearest negative foil (neg_4) has the same coarse two-loop rectangle/sector contact but the two exterior openings are much more balanced; other negatives lack the unique two-loop signature or have additional loops. The asymmetry likely needs both an absolute narrow-gap constraint and a relative imbalance constraint, while the broad gap helps reject geometrically compressed distractors.

intents.rationale: At the positive junctions, one of the two exterior gaps is consistently narrow; this captures the tight side of the contact and helps separate the balanced nearest foil.
The other exterior gap in positives remains substantially open, complementing the narrow-gap condition and excluding contacts where both openings are compressed.
The positive contacts are characterized by pronounced inequality between the two exterior gaps, whereas the nearest two-loop negative foil has comparatively similar openings.
